title: Gastroenterology Fellowship
inst: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (Harvard Medical School)
Department: Division of Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Summary: BIDMC's ACGME gastroenterology fellowship trains physicians over three years for careers in academic gastroenterology and hepatology, with dedicated time tailored to each fellow's goals in clinical care, research and education.

title: Advanced Endoscopy Fellowship
inst: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (Harvard Medical School)
Department: Center for Advanced Endoscopy, Division of Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition
Duration: 1 year (some fellows elect additional time for clinical training or research)
Eligibility: Completion of a gastroenterology fellowship and standard application materials.
International applicants: A sponsored position is available for qualified international/domestic applicants in addition to two ASGE-matched positions.
Positions: Two ASGE-matched positions plus one sponsored position
Summary: Rigorous one-year training in modern advanced endoscopy at New England's largest ERCP referral practice, with a core focus on pancreaticobiliary endoscopy, diagnostic and interventional EUS, EMR and novel techniques.

title: Advanced Hepatology Fellowship
inst: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (Harvard Medical School)
Department: The Liver Center, Division of Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition
Eligibility: Open to graduates of internal medicine residency programmes.
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Application method: Email personal statement and three recommendation letters (one from most recent programme director) to the fellowship coordinator
Positions: 1 per year (the department overview page states two positions)
Summary: One-year training of gastroenterologists in hepatology and liver transplantation at a centre performing about 40 liver transplants a year, with a focus on developing academic leaders.

title: Transplant Hepatology Fellowship
inst: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (Harvard Medical School)
Department: The Liver Center, Division of Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition
Duration: 1 year (fourth year after GI fellowship; internal applicants may combine GI-transplant hepatology in 3 years)
Eligibility: Completion of gastroenterology fellowship (or internal combined pathway).
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited; meets ABIM board eligibility requirements in transplant hepatology
Application method: Email CV, personal statement and 3 letters of recommendation to the programme director via coordinator
Summary: One-year ACGME-accredited programme offering intensive inpatient and outpatient training in liver transplant and advanced liver disease care, leading to ABIM transplant hepatology board eligibility and UNOS certification.

title: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) Fellowship
inst: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (Harvard Medical School)
Department: Center for Inflammatory Bowel Disease, Division of Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition
Deadline: Applications accepted through December 2026; interviews January 2027
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Accreditation: Reviewed and recognised by the BIDMC Graduate Medical Education Committee (non-ACGME)
Funding: Supported by educational grants from IBD-Start (Crohn's and Colitis Foundation), Janssen Scientific Affairs and AbbVie
Summary: Structured advanced training to develop academic gastroenterologists expert in managing complex IBD at one of the region's largest IBD practices (over 4,000 patients).

title: Gastroenterology Fellowship
inst: Boston Medical Center / Boston University Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine
Department: Section of Gastroenterology
Duration: 3 years (18 months clinical training mandatory; year 1 clinical, years 2-3 mainly research)
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Application method: ERAS; NRMP Match (clinical and research positions placed in the Match)
Summary: Three-year fellowship combining clinical activities, procedural training, an educational curriculum and mentored research at Boston Medical Center and the Boston VA Medical Center.

title: Advanced Inflammatory Bowel Disease Fellowship
inst: Boston Medical Center / Boston University Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine
Department: IBD Center, Section of Gastroenterology
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Summary: An additional year of multidisciplinary IBD training at the BMC IBD Center to prepare GI fellows for careers as IBD clinicians or clinical investigators.

title: Gastroenterology and Hepatology Fellowship
inst: Weill Cornell Medicine / NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital
Department: Division of Gastroenterology & Hepatology, Weill Department of Medicine
Deadline: Applications accepted July-August 2026; interviews 28 September, 2 October and 6 October 2026
Eligibility: Complete ERAS application package required; training satisfies ABIM requirements for gastroenterology.
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Summary: A three-year programme at NewYork-Presbyterian/Weill Cornell that seeks trainees interested in academic medicine, with extensive interaction with GI pathologists, radiologists and surgeons and rotations through busy ERCP and EUS services.

title: Advanced Endoscopy Fellowship
inst: Weill Cornell Medicine / NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital
Department: Division of Gastroenterology & Hepatology, Weill Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Completion of a three-year ABIM-certified academic gastroenterology fellowship within five years of application; U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
International applicants: Not eligible unless U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
Funding: Fellowship salary support is generated by the trainee through one day per week of general endoscopy procedures.
Visa support: No - due to funding restrictions, applicants with J-1 or H-1B visas are not eligible to apply.
Summary: A one-year fourth-year programme giving expert-level cognitive and technical training in EUS, ERCP, third-space endoscopy and endobariatrics to train future leaders in academic endoscopy.

title: Transplant Hepatology Fellowship
inst: Weill Cornell Medicine / NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital
Department: Center for Liver Disease and Transplantation (combined with Columbia University Irving Medical Center)
Deadline: Applications open January; interviews March-April; match in May (2026 cycle stated)
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited combined programme at NewYork-Presbyterian across Weill Cornell and Columbia, providing intensive clinical training in liver transplant care, education and research.

title: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) Fellowship
inst: Weill Cornell Medicine / NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital
Department: Jill Roberts Center for Inflammatory Bowel Disease, Division of Gastroenterology & Hepatology
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Application method: Complete and return the programme application form
Summary: An intensive multidisciplinary one-year programme, begun in 2019, developing expertise in IBD patient care and research in line with Crohn's and Colitis Foundation guidance.

title: Gastroenterology and Hepatology Fellowship
inst: Montefiore Einstein (Montefiore Medical Center / Albert Einstein College of Medicine)
Department: Division of Gastroenterology and Liver Diseases, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Completion of an accredited three-year internal medicine programme.
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Application method: ERAS (follows ERAS deadlines; no supplemental information required)
Summary: A three-year programme offering vast clinical and endoscopic experience, with fellows rotating through five hospitals (including Moses, Weiler, Jacobi and Wakefield campuses) alongside more than 25 faculty.

title: Advanced Clinical Hepatology Fellowship
inst: University of Toronto / University Health Network (Toronto General Hospital)
Department: Division of Gastroenterology & Hepatology, Department of Medicine; Liver Clinic, Toronto General Hospital
Deadline: Applications accepted throughout the year but must be received 12 months before start date
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: International applicants who meet CPSO requirements for licensure as a clinical fellow may contact the fellowship programme director; trainees from countries with University of Toronto postgraduate training agreements apply via their sponsoring agency.
Accreditation: University of Toronto Department of Medicine clinical fellowship (PGME-registered; not RCPSC-certifying)
Visa support: PGME provides successful international applicants with documentation to apply for the appropriate Canadian work permit.
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for a CPSO certificate authorizing postgraduate education (educational licence); applicants must be recognised as specialists in the jurisdiction where they practised before the fellowship.
Summary: A one-year clinical hepatology fellowship in Ontario's largest liver unit, centred on ambulatory general hepatology, viral hepatitis and autoimmune liver disease with supervision of inpatient hepatology consult services.

title: Advanced Endoscopy Fellowship
inst: University of Toronto / University Health Network (Toronto General and Toronto Western Hospitals)
Department: Division of Gastroenterology & Hepatology, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: International applicants who meet CPSO requirements for licensure as a clinical fellow may contact the fellowship programme director; trainees from countries with University of Toronto postgraduate training agreements apply via their sponsoring agency.
Accreditation: University of Toronto Department of Medicine clinical fellowship (PGME-registered; not RCPSC-certifying)
Visa support: PGME provides successful international applicants with documentation to apply for the appropriate Canadian work permit.
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for a CPSO certificate authorizing postgraduate education (educational licence); applicants must be recognised as specialists in the jurisdiction where they practised before the fellowship.
Summary: A one-year fellowship at Toronto General and Toronto Western Hospitals training fellows to independently perform ERCP and EUS, with protected research time.

title: Inflammatory Bowel Disease Clinical/Research Fellowship (Women's College Hospital)
inst: University of Toronto / Women's College Hospital
Department: Division of Gastroenterology, Women's College Hospital
Duration: 1 year (option of one to two years)
Eligibility: Completion of a gastroenterology residency/fellowship.
International applicants: International applicants who meet CPSO requirements for licensure as a clinical fellow may contact the fellowship programme director; trainees from countries with University of Toronto postgraduate training agreements apply via their sponsoring agency.
Accreditation: University of Toronto Department of Medicine clinical fellowship (PGME-registered; not RCPSC-certifying)
Application method: Send CV and cover letter to the fellowship contact
Visa support: PGME provides successful international applicants with documentation to apply for the appropriate Canadian work permit.
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for a CPSO certificate authorizing postgraduate education (educational licence); applicants must be recognised as specialists in the jurisdiction where they practised before the fellowship.
Summary: A primarily ambulatory clinical/research IBD fellowship at Women's College Hospital, including IBD endoscopy and six weeks of inpatient service at Sunnybrook, with a clinical research project ideally within a Master's programme.

title: Inflammatory Bowel Disease Fellowship (St. Michael's Hospital)
inst: University of Toronto / St. Michael's Hospital (Unity Health Toronto)
Department: Division of Gastroenterology, St. Michael's Hospital
Eligibility: Completion of a gastroenterology residency/fellowship.
International applicants: International applicants who meet CPSO requirements for licensure as a clinical fellow may contact the fellowship programme director; trainees from countries with University of Toronto postgraduate training agreements apply via their sponsoring agency.
Accreditation: University of Toronto Department of Medicine clinical fellowship (PGME-registered; not RCPSC-certifying)
Visa support: PGME provides successful international applicants with documentation to apply for the appropriate Canadian work permit.
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for a CPSO certificate authorizing postgraduate education (educational licence); applicants must be recognised as specialists in the jurisdiction where they practised before the fellowship.
Summary: A clinical/research IBD fellowship at St. Michael's Hospital, an OMED/WGO world centre of excellence, with a focus on IBD endoscopy including stricture management and chromoendoscopy.

title: Neurogastroenterology and Motility Fellowship
inst: University of Toronto / University Health Network
Department: Division of Gastroenterology & Hepatology, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: International applicants who meet CPSO requirements for licensure as a clinical fellow may contact the fellowship programme director; trainees from countries with University of Toronto postgraduate training agreements apply via their sponsoring agency.
Accreditation: University of Toronto Department of Medicine clinical fellowship (PGME-registered; not RCPSC-certifying)

Summary: A one-year clinical fellowship building expertise in neurogastroenterology and motility, including performing and interpreting GI motility testing and managing functional bowel disease.

title: Clinical Nutrition Fellowship
inst: University of Toronto / University Health Network (Toronto General Hospital)
Department: Division of Gastroenterology & Hepatology, Department of Medicine
Duration: 1-2 years (6-12 months mentored clinical training; additional time for research)
Eligibility: Completion of categorical residency training (e.g. internal medicine, surgery, paediatrics, or subspecialty training such as gastroenterology, endocrinology, critical care, nephrology or cardiology).
International applicants: International applicants who meet CPSO requirements for licensure as a clinical fellow may contact the fellowship programme director; trainees from countries with University of Toronto postgraduate training agreements apply via their sponsoring agency.
Accreditation: University of Toronto Department of Medicine clinical fellowship (PGME-registered; not RCPSC-certifying)
Visa support: PGME provides successful international applicants with documentation to apply for the appropriate Canadian work permit.
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for a CPSO certificate authorizing postgraduate education (educational licence); applicants must be recognised as specialists in the jurisdiction where they practised before the fellowship.
Summary: Training to competency as a specialist in clinical nutrition through mentored inpatient and outpatient experience, formal instruction and a clinical research project.

title: Therapeutic Endoscopy Fellowship
inst: University of Toronto / St. Michael's Hospital (Unity Health Toronto)
Department: Division of Gastroenterology, St. Michael's Hospital
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: International applicants who meet CPSO requirements for licensure as a clinical fellow may contact the fellowship programme director; trainees from countries with University of Toronto postgraduate training agreements apply via their sponsoring agency.
Accreditation: University of Toronto Department of Medicine clinical fellowship (PGME-registered; not RCPSC-certifying)
Visa support: PGME provides successful international applicants with documentation to apply for the appropriate Canadian work permit.
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for a CPSO certificate authorizing postgraduate education (educational licence); applicants must be recognised as specialists in the jurisdiction where they practised before the fellowship.
Summary: A comprehensive advanced endoscopy fellowship at Canada's largest therapeutic endoscopy referral centre, covering ERCP with cholangioscopy, diagnostic and therapeutic EUS, EMR, stenting, RFA and double-balloon enteroscopy.

title: Transplant Hepatology Fellowship
inst: University of Toronto / University Health Network (Toronto General Hospital)
Department: Multi-Organ Transplant Program and Division of Gastroenterology & Hepatology
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: International applicants who meet CPSO requirements for licensure as a clinical fellow may contact the fellowship programme director; trainees from countries with University of Toronto postgraduate training agreements apply via their sponsoring agency.
Accreditation: University of Toronto Department of Medicine clinical fellowship (PGME-registered; not RCPSC-certifying)
Funding: Salary approximately CAD 85,000 (includes in-house multi-organ transplant call 2-3 times per month)
Visa support: PGME provides successful international applicants with documentation to apply for the appropriate Canadian work permit.
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for a CPSO certificate authorizing postgraduate education (educational licence); applicants must be recognised as specialists in the jurisdiction where they practised before the fellowship.
Summary: Fully funded transplant hepatology fellowship at a centre performing about 200 adult liver transplants a year (25-30% living donor), rotating through inpatient, outpatient and research weeks.

title: Hepatology Training Program
inst: University of British Columbia / Vancouver General Hospital
Department: Division of Gastroenterology, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Completion of gastroenterology or internal medicine training with an interest in liver disease.
International applicants: Welcomes both Canadian and international trainees.
Accreditation: Fulfils RCPSC Area of Focused Competence (AFC) Diploma in Hepatology requirements; alumni eligible for the diploma via the RCPSC practice route
Application method: Contact the programme director or programme coordinator by email
Summary: A Vancouver General Hospital-based hepatology programme (since 1999) developing inpatient and outpatient expertise in liver transplantation, portal hypertension, acute liver failure, viral hepatitis and HCC.

title: Advanced Fellowship in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
inst: University of British Columbia / St. Paul's Hospital (Providence Health Care)
Department: Division of Gastroenterology, St. Paul's Hospital
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Summary: An advanced IBD fellowship at St. Paul's Hospital, a leading Canadian academic IBD centre, providing clinical exposure and a research foundation structured around CanMEDS roles.

title: Therapeutic Endoscopy Fellowship
inst: University of British Columbia (Vancouver General Hospital and St. Paul's Hospital)
Department: Division of Gastroenterology, Department of Medicine
Duration: 1 year (6 months each at Vancouver General and St Paul's)
Eligibility: Candidates generally already have some ERCP and/or EUS training.
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Summary: An intensive one-year ERCP/EUS fellowship (close to 1,000 ERCPs and over 700 EUS per fellow) including EUS-guided drainage, necrosectomy, enteral stenting and cholangioscopy.

title: Fellowship in Advanced Colorectal Therapeutics (FACT)
inst: University of Calgary (Cumming School of Medicine)
Department: Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology; Forzani & MacPhail Colon Cancer Screening Centre
Deadline: 31 May the year prior to start; interviews typically June/July
Eligibility: Graduates of adult gastroenterology and colorectal surgery training programmes.
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Summary: A fellowship developing leaders in colonoscopy and advanced colorectal tissue resection at a high-volume screening centre performing about 17,500 colonoscopies a year, with the option of a graduate degree.

title: Gastrointestinal Motility Fellowship
inst: University of Calgary (Cumming School of Medicine)
Department: Calgary Gut Motility Centre, South Health Campus
Deadline: 1 November the year prior to fellowship start
Eligibility: Completion of internal medicine and gastroenterology residency training.
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Application method: Email CV and letter of intent to the GI programme administrator
Funding: Self-funded: proof of external financial support (institution, award, grant or bursary) of CAD 60,000 or more is required; salary support at PGY-6 level.
Summary: A one-year clinical and academic motility fellowship at the Calgary Gut Motility Centre, interpreting nearly 2,000 motility tests a year (HRM, impedance-pH, BRAVO, endoFLIP) with a required motility research project.

title: Inflammatory Bowel Disease Fellowship
inst: University of Calgary (Cumming School of Medicine)
Department: Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology; Inflammatory Bowel Disease Group
Eligibility: Completion of an accredited gastroenterology training programme with demonstrated interest in IBD.
International applicants: Applications considered from applicants of any nationality provided they are eligible for licensure as trainees in Canada.
Accreditation: University of Calgary certificate (IBD training is not RCPSC-accredited)
Funding: Funded position with salary commensurate with PGY-6 on the PARA scale
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for licensure as a trainee in Canada (Alberta).
Summary: A 12-month funded programme developing clinical and research expertise in IBD through 4-5 dedicated IBD clinics a week, IBD endoscopy and a major research project.

title: Therapeutic Endoscopy Fellowship
inst: University of Calgary (Cumming School of Medicine)
Department: Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology (Peter Lougheed Centre)
Duration: 1-2 years (two-year candidates with concurrent graduate degree prioritised)
Deadline: 31 March the year prior to fellowship start; interviews late May/early June
Eligibility: Training in basic endoscopy (gastroscopy and colonoscopy) required; typically trained gastroenterologists, general surgeons also welcomed.
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Application method: Application documents plus 3 reference letters sent directly by referees to the GI programme administrator
Funding: Fully funded by the Pentax Advanced Therapeutic Endoscopy Fellowship Award, up to CAD 75,000/year
Summary: An academically oriented ERCP/EUS and luminal therapeutics fellowship with about 1,600 ERCPs and 1,300 EUS a year and mandatory research.

title: International Trainee Fellowship in Gastroenterology
inst: St Mark's Hospital (London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust) / St Mark's Academic Institute
Department: St Mark's Academic Institute
Duration: Minimum 3 months; typically 6-12 months; maximum 2 years
Eligibility: Suitably qualified international medical graduates (postgraduate doctors) seeking structured subspecialty training in gastroenterology or coloproctology.
International applicants: Yes - programme is designed for international medical graduates; fellows attached to a consultant supervisor and do not undertake unsupervised patient care or on-call duties.
Accreditation: Royal College-supported International Trainee Fellowship (not a UK specialty training post)
Application method: Apply online via St Mark's Academic Institute
Funding: Self-funded; fees GBP 4,300 (3-6 months) or GBP 6,500 (7-12 months)
Visa support: Operates under the UK Tier 5 (Temporary Worker) visa within the points-based immigration system.
Licence requirement: Must be registered with one of the Royal Colleges, which sponsors GMC registration with a licence to practise.
Summary: A Royal College-supported programme giving international doctors structured, hands-on subspecialty training in gastroenterology or coloproctology under consultant supervision at St Mark's, with access to academic meetings and research.

title: Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition Fellowship
inst: University of Chicago Medicine
Department: Section of Gastroenterology, Hepatology & Nutrition, Department of Medicine
Duration: 3 years (minimum 18 months clinical; Clinical Scholars and Research Scholars tracks)
Eligibility: Not stated on official page
International applicants: Not stated on official page
Funding: Research track supported by the longest continuously funded NIH T32 training grant in gastroenterology in the US
Summary: A three-year ACGME fellowship with Clinical Scholars and Research Scholars tracks providing comprehensive clinical, endoscopic and research training; about 75% of graduates pursue academic careers.

title: Advanced Fellowship in Transplant Hepatology
inst: University of Chicago Medicine
Department: Section of Gastroenterology, Hepatology & Nutrition, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Completion of, or enrolment in, a three-year gastroenterology fellowship.
International applicants: Non-U.S. citizens must meet appropriate visa requirements.
Visa support: Not stated on official page (applicants must meet appropriate visa requirements if non-U.S. citizen or immigrant)
Licence requirement: Valid Illinois medical licence (application may be pending)
Summary: A 12-month ACGME-accredited fellowship giving focused clinical and research training in liver disease and liver transplantation as a third-tier experience for future hepatologists.

title: Advanced Fellowship in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
inst: University of Chicago Medicine
Department: Inflammatory Bowel Disease Center, Section of Gastroenterology, Hepatology & Nutrition
Start: Next available position: academic year 2029-2030 (2027-2029 positions full)
Deadline: Applications for 2029 accepted from 1 November 2027; reviewed on receipt
Eligibility: Completion of internal medicine and gastroenterology training at accredited institutions (or equivalent if non-US trained).
International applicants: Non-US/Canadian citizens must obtain appropriate visa and ECFMG certification in advance of application.
Licence requirement: Illinois medical licence (may be pending at application; required to start)
Summary: An additional year of individualised clinical, translational or basic research training in IBD at a large quaternary IBD referral centre.

title: Advanced Fellowship in Interventional Endoscopy
inst: University of Chicago Medicine
Department: Interventional Endoscopy Service, Section of Gastroenterology, Hepatology & Nutrition
Eligibility: Completion of a three-year gastroenterology training programme (board eligible/certified).
International applicants: Non-U.S. citizens must meet appropriate visa requirements (ECFMG).
Licence requirement: Illinois medical licence (application may be pending)
Summary: A one-year hands-on interventional endoscopy fellowship covering GI oncology and advanced endoscopic techniques, with expected research output (DDW abstract and ASGE video).

title: Fellowship in Clinical Nutrition and Small Bowel Disease
inst: University of Chicago Medicine
Department: Section of Gastroenterology, Hepatology & Nutrition, Department of Medicine
Eligibility: Completion of internal medicine training at an ACGME-accredited institution (or equivalent if non-US trained).
International applicants: Non-U.S. citizens need appropriate visa and ECFMG certification.
Licence requirement: Illinois medical licence (may be pending at application; required to start)
Summary: An individualised clinical nutrition and small bowel disease programme for trainees seeking an academic appointment, closely associated with the ACGME GI fellowship.
